item.title: France's top court blocks under-15 social media ban, citing constitutional freedoms
item.description:
France’s Constitutional Council has blocked a bill that would have banned social media access for under-15s, ruling that it infringed on freedom of expression. It’s a setback for President Emmanuel Macron, who has championed the legislation and has now asked his prime minister to rewrite the bill. The Élysée says Macron remains determined to have the reform in place before next year’s presidential election. France 24 International Affairs editor tells us more.

item.title: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
item.description:
Zambia's electoral commission on Friday suspended vote counting from Thursday's presidential and parliamentary elections for at least 24 hours due to “violence targeted at poll staff” and reported instances of theft of marked ballot papers. Former minister Brian Mundubile, the main challenger to President Hakainde Hichilema, claimed a first-round victory and said his camp viewed "the continued delay ... with grave concern".

item.title: What’s next for far-right Reform UK after Farage’s by-election win?
item.description:
A small British seaside town voted Thursday in a special election between a hard-right populist and a man who wears a trash can on his head. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage resigned to call the by-election after being accused of accepting an unlawful gift, but no major parties ran against him , and one of British politics’ many novelty candidates, Count Binface, is his only noteworthy opponent. It is “ an unserious politics for a time of decadence ,” an observer wrote in The New York Times; Farage will likely win, but at some cost to his reputation. Adding to Reform’s woes, their recent nationwide poll lead has evaporated, with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham boosting incumbent Labour’s standing. — Tom Chivers

item.title: ‘Unprecedented’ rain kills five in Japan as thousands stranded at airport
item.description:
Evacuation orders issued for 400,000 after flooding, landslide warnings and power outages in Chiba prefecture At least five people have died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain that left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings. The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Thursday night, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. Evacuation orders were issued for more than 400,000 people in Chiba and other areas, and about 45,000 homes lost power, as 115mm of rain fell hourly, approximately the same amount usually recorded for the whole month of August. item.description:

item.title: Hawaii braces for direct hit from Tropical Storm Lala
item.description:
Storm expected to strengthen to hurricane as state of emergency declared amid danger of ‘life-threatening’ floods Tropical Storm Lala is set to hit Hawaii’s Big Island with hurricane force in a matter of hours, bringing dangerous winds, heavy rainfall and high surf in a sign of what a strengthening “super” El Niño in the Pacific may bring. The tropical storm is currently about 420 miles (675km) south-east of Hilo on the archipelago’s largest island, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) said in its latest advisory, packing winds of 60mph (97km/h). Lala is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane as it approaches the Big Island. Continue reading...

item.title: British cyclist Finlay Tarling dies in Tour of Portugal crash aged 19
item.description:
Finlay Tarling, a rider with the NSN Development team, has died following a crash on stage 8 of the Volta a Portugal, the race announced Friday. Tarling was 19. The statement from the race read: “The organization of the 87th Volta a Portugal em Bicicleta Jogos Santa Casa deeply regrets to announce the passing of British cyclist Finlay Tarling, from the NSN Development Team, following a serious accident that occurred during the 8th stage of the race. In light of this tragic event, the race will be neutralized until reaching Fafe and, as a sign of respect and mourning, the podium ceremony scheduled for today will not take place.” Tarling raced for Great Britain on the road and track alongside his brother Josh, who races for Netcompany-Ineos. item.title: Congo: Ebola cases are rising at record pace
item.description:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo spread to a sixth province as the overall death toll surpassed 2,100 and cases topped 4,500. Experts say the virus may have been transmitted undetected for months, while health workers have struggled to contain the outbreak with poor medical supplies and no approved vaccine for the new strain — though several are in the works. The head of the World Health Organization this week warned that the current outbreak threatens to be the biggest ever, with authorities playing catch-up to the disease after “ a big head start. ” During the previous deadliest outbreak, which killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016, authorities had recorded 755 cases at the same point . — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Fifth Circuit Allows 2021 Texas Election Integrity Law To Finally Go Into Effect
item.description:
The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals restored key parts of Texas’ election law Wednesday, handing the state a major win after repeatedly reversing the lower court during a five-year legal fight. The 11-page ruling overturned a lower court decision that blocked nine parts of Senate Bill 1, a 2021 law that changed Texas’ rules for mail-in voting and voter assistance. The appeals court pointed to its repeated reversals in the case, noting that it has "reversed the district court on everything" during roughly five years of litigation. item.title: Baby with heart defect at center of US surrogacy dispute handed to parents
item.description:
Biological parents given custody of child born in Texas amid dispute over surrogate mother’s claim of abortion request A two-day-old baby with a rare heart defect at the center of a complex surrogacy dispute in Texas has been handed over to the parents’ custody and is receiving care, lawyers for the parents said on Friday. The baby has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a defect that requires surgeries to correct. The baby was born on Wednesday to surrogate mother McKenna West of Alaska after she reportedly refused requests to get an abortion from the biological parents, Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed of California – requests they deny making.
